top.title: Victor Wembanyama delivers message against Luka Dončić and the Lakers in MVP showdown
top.description: SAN ANTONIO — Mitch Johnson didn’t have much use for his clipboard at the moment. The Spurs head coach sat in the middle of the huddle with a crowd around him, gesturing flagrantly with a 17-point deficit staring his team in the face. No X’s-and-O’s pep talk was necessary; Johnson was demonstrating how his players needed to respond to the Lakers’ force. A message heard by many was truly intended for one very tall alien. On Friday, every step Victor Wembanyama took was met with more resistance than Agent J and Agent K from Men in Black . The men in purple had made it very clear from the opening tip of their intention to rough Wembanyama up. Pressure in the backcourt. Pressure in the frontcourt. Double teams. Fronting him with a second — and sometimes a third — helper rotating over the second his hands touched the ball. The old Wemby might have wilted, faded away as the game wore on, frustrated with the overwhelming physicality. This updated version simply downloads the data and adjusts like artificial intelligence. So the Spurs stormed back in the second half, and with the game hanging in the balance, it was Wembanyama who answered brute force’s call. At one end, the Frenchman barrelled through Luka Dončić and Walker Kessler en route to the rim for an emphatic slam. Seconds later, he darted to the restricted area, leaping as high as his limbs and outstretched fingertips could go, sending Collin Sexton’s shot all the way back to La Brea. Message received. “There was some maturity tonight that was good to see,” Johnson said following the 99-96 win , which earned the Spurs a spot in the NBA Cup quarterfinals . “When things aren’t going well, there are some things you can’t control. But I thought we did a good job of working the game, staying in the game. It was a good step against a very high-level team.” Friday night — or the latest reboot of Alien vs. Predator — was a celebration of differences. On one hand, this was the apex of Western Conference talent, a showdown of Wembanyama and Dončić, MVP favorites who do their respective damage in contrasting styles and their relationship with space. Dončić, the swashbuckling offensive hub that has mastered the art of manipulating areas around him, against Wembanyama, the defensive wizard who can magnify or minimize game plans on a whim. On the other hand, it was unique insight into Wembanyama’s growth and exactly what sets him apart from his peers. This game was not aesthetically pleasing. No team shot better than 50% from the field, 35% from deep or even 75% from the charity stripe. There were 39 combined turnovers and 32 fouls. Dončić finished with 31 points on 31 shots, Wembanyama ended up with 25 points on 25 shots. But even amidst the ugliness, beauty can be uncovered. The postgame locker room mood suggested as much, with the Spurs fully understanding the Lakers’ unique, aggressive approach to Wembanyama. top.title: INEC, security agencies addressing security concerns ahead of 2027 polls – Amupitan
top.description: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, says the commission, in collaboration with security agencies, is taking necessary steps to address all security concerns ahead of the 2027 general elections. Amupitan ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​⁠‌‌‍‍‌‌​stated this on Saturday in Jos while speaking with newsmen during the monitoring of the ongoing mock accreditation. Addressing a question on the security challenge and the likely implications on voter participation, Amupitan said the safety of ad hoc staff and all Nigerians remained a priority to the commission. “As the chairman of INEC, I’m also worried about the state of security in Nigeria, but you can see we are taking some good steps to ensure that we nip it in the bud. “Just two days ago, we had a national security conference where we brought together all the members of the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES), the police, the military, the Civil Defence, and other paramilitary agencies. “So, we had a one-day conference where we discussed all these issues,” he said. Amupitan said that INEC had conducted a risk assessment of every part of Nigeria, using Election Risk Management (ERM) tools. “We have identified all the polling units that are vulnerable, and we have shared this with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extraordinary preparation for those places. “Any polling unit 500 meters from those vulnerable areas has been identified, and we are going to deal with it,” he said. Amupitan said the commission was interested in the security of the voters and ad hoc staff, particularly corps members. “It’s not every security matter you can bring to the open, but we are doing everything, both intelligence and physical, to ensure that the security on election day is assured,” he said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the monitoring of the mock accreditation exercise was still ongoing in different parts of the state as of the time of filling this report. top.title: Electricity’ll improve, Mbah and I are working on Eastern Gas Pipeline – Tinubu
top.description: President Bola Tinubu has said electricity supply will improve in the South-East, adding that his administration has approved the Eastern Gas Pipeline and Eastern Nigeria rail line as part of plans to boost infrastructure and connectivity in the region. Tinubu made the remarks on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Enugu, where he said he was working with Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah on the gas pipeline project. “Electricity will improve. The Eastern Gas Pipeline is approved. Peter Mbah and I are working on it,” the president said. He also announced the approval of the Eastern Nigeria rail line, saying the projects would improve connections between the South-East, South-South and northern parts of the country. “Also approved is the Eastern Nigeria rail line. We will connect you, connect the East, South and North. It’s our honest promise for development,” he said. Addressing farmers in the region, Tinubu promised interest-free loans and financial support, alongside measures to reduce the challenges associated with farming. “To our farmers, they will receive money, loans that are interest-free. We will relieve them of the burdens of farming. We will connect with infrastructure,” he said. The president also urged residents to participate in the January 16 election, asking them to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and turn out to vote for the APC. “January 16, you must go out and vote. Take your friends, take your brothers, take your sisters. You must collect your PVC and go there, for President, vote APC, for honourable, APC,” Tinubu said. top.title: Duda Sampaio on Japan friendly: “We’re expecting a great game”
top.description: Duda Sampaio on Japan friendly: “We’re expecting a great game” The Brazilian women's national team faces Japan this Sunday (29) at 1:55 a.m. Brasília time at Edion Peace Wing Stadium in Hiroshima, in the team's penultimate match of the 2026 season. After the final training session before the match, midfielder Duda Sampaio looked ahead to the encounter and highlighted the importance of facing a team familiar with Brazil's approach. “We're really looking forward to it. It's the last national team camp of the year, and we're very aware that the World Cup is getting closer and closer. Japan is a familiar opponent, so I think that's good for us, but they should bring something new. Having faced us several times, they also know our style of play well, so I think they could pose challenges, and that's good for our preparation. We're expecting a great match. These are two very strong teams, but if all goes well, we'll come away with the win,” she said. Brazil's players began arriving in Japan on November 22. Although on-field training began on Wednesday (25), the coaching staff organized a series of activities to help the players adjust more quickly and easily to the time difference and the Japanese climate. Duda gave a positive assessment of the preparation period and highlighted how well the team had used its time. “The adjustment went really well. From the first training sessions, we managed to settle in well and get some rest so that, when we got onto the pitch, we could make the most of our training right away. It was a very productive week. We always have limited time here, so we try to make the most of training sessions and meetings,” she explained. Duda Sampaio during a Brazil training session in Hiroshima Credits: Luciana Vermell/CBF Duda Sampaio was announced as a Corinthians signing in late 2022 and has experienced Arthur Elias's work firsthand ever since. The coach left the São Paulo club in 2023 to take charge of the Brazilian national team, and the midfielder, who had already worked with him, became a regular in the Brazil squad. Having been part of that journey makes the milestone of 50 matches in charge of the team, which the coach will reach this Sunday, all the more special. Duda, who earned her 50th Brazil cap in June 2026, highlighted the relationship they have built over the years and her happiness at being part of the process. “I'm very happy to have followed Arthur's work from Corinthians through to his arrival here. For me, experiencing that was very special. We exchange ideas a lot, and I know his work, his way of thinking and him as a person very well. It's a joy to be able to benefit from that here. He's reaching 50 matches, but I'm sure we'll have many more ahead of us, because we know how seriously he takes his work, and it shows all of Brazil that we're on the right track to achieve our goals,” she concluded. top.title: NC State takes down Kansas State, 85-70
top.description: RALEIGH, NC - NOVEMBER 19: Qadence Samuels #2 of the NC State Wolfpack shoots over Johnea Donahue #3 of the Georgetown Hoyas during the college basketball game between the Georgetown Hoyas and the NC State Wolfpack on November 19, 2026 at Reynolds Coliseum in Raleigh, NC. (Photo by Nicholas Faulkner/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The shots were falling for both teams on Friday night, which made for an entertaining back and forth that lasted about three quarters—before NC State finally seized control for good. It wasn’t exactly a defensive clinic for either team, not surprisingly, as both hit the 40-point mark in the first half. Wes Moore wasn’t super thrilled about the effort by his team on defense, but it did make for a fun half to watch. The Pack did get a bit better there in the second half, while Kansas State did not. The Wildcats played zone for the entire evening, mixing up some looks here and there, but mostly sticking with a 2-3 that left such spacious gaps that I’m sure Jim Boeheim was turning over in his grave. Qadence Samuels took advantage by doing her best Paul McNeil impression—she was 6-8 from three, and the team finished 10-15 from outside. As you can tell from that attempt total, NC State did not force the issue from the perimeter against K-State’s zone, mostly because that wasn’t necessary, as getting paint touches was still pretty easy. Zoe Brooks was back on the court for the first time in nearly three weeks and was back to her usual playmaking self, if maybe still a step slow. She had a beautiful dish to Khamil Pierre for a bucket to beat the third quarter horn that was part of an 11-0 run that put Kansas State in the rearview for good. That included the first seven points of the fourth quarter, five of which belonged to Brooks. The Pack ended up leading by double figures for the final nine minutes. Desiree Wooten put together another outstanding performance, scoring 21 points on 8-9 shooting; Khamil Pierre led all scorers with 23 points on 9-15 shooting. Samuels finished with 20. A good result for the Pack against a potential NCAA tournament team (K-State is No. 56 in Torvik), but the big test comes Saturday afternoon against LSU and the evil Mrs. SparkleFeathers.

In fact, for the next few hours, I would prefer not to discuss the merits of his continued employment at all, because we have far more pressing business to attend to: beating That Team Up North. Believe me, I am well aware of how frustrating, disappointing, and downright demoralizing this Ohio State football season has been. I have spilled more than my fair share of digital ink lamenting the state of the program, questioning the decisions of its leadership, and wondering what needs to change to get the Buckeyes back to where we all believe they belong. I stand by those sentiments, and I suspect that I will feel just as strongly about them when I wake up on Sunday morning. But Sunday is not today, and there is nothing that you, I, or anyone else outside of that locker room can do between now and the final whistle to address the issues that have plagued this program. So, I am imploring every member of Buckeye Nation to temporarily set aside our perfectly legitimate grievances, suspend our cynicism, and embrace the unbridled, unapologetic, occasionally irrational passion that comes with being a fan in the greatest rivalry in all of sports. top.title: Luka Dončić gets in physical confrontation with fan
top.description: Credit: Amazon Prime Video It was a bizarre scene in San Antonio as Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić got into a physical confrontation with a fan seated on the baseline. The Lakers held a 16-point halftime lead against the Spurs in their NBA Cup matchup on Friday night, but San Antonio rallied in the second half for a 99-96 victory. Dončić was visibly frustrated as he shot just 1-13 from downtown. He’s been scoring at such a historic rate this season that his 31 points were five off his season average. After the game was over and Luka was walking to the locker room, he took off his elbow band and threw it at a woman seated on the baseline who appeared to be yelling at him. Dončić then went back for the elbow band and the man seated next to her (presumably her husband or a significant other) then shoved Luka before a horde of people intervened to prevent the situation from escalating further. The camera above the backboard captured it all on the Amazon Prime Video telecast. A fan shoved Luka after he threw his band toward them https://t.co/AKh93Z9QUK — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) November 28, 2026 Luka Dončić is prone to the occasional outburst and his behavior has drawn criticism over the years at various points throughout his career . But this was a regrettable and bizarre incident that was easily preventable. The first fan was clearly letting Luka have it while walking to the locker room, but Dončić should know better and not engage by throwing anything at her. If he just ignored it, then none of what followed would have happened. Going back for the elbow band he threw was another strange decision. As for the male fan, you can appreciate him standing up for the lady, but there’s no excuse for ever putting your hands on a player. Thankfully it didn’t rise to Malice in the Palace levels or anything, but everyone was in the wrong here. top.title: Red Sox's Triston Casas Could Force Interesting Lineup Decision Amid Return
top.description: Red Sox's Triston Casas Could Force Interesting Lineup Decision Amid Return originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Red Sox have spent years trying to sort out their first base and designated hitter situation, hoping Triston Casas would eventually be the answer. Unfortunately for the Red Sox and Casas, injuries have derailed that a bit. As a result, the Red Sox have had to make moves, landing William Contreras last offseason and signing Jake Bauers this winter. A healthy Casas changes the lineup, especially if he can return to the player that we saw back in 2023. While the injuries certainly haven't helped Casas over the past couple of seasons now, there's no debating how good he was in 2023, hitting 24 home runs, 21 doubles, and driving in 65 runs. He returned to action in a winter ball game in the DR, playing Friday and hitting a grand slam. Casas also has a ton of upside. He has legitimate power in his left-handed bat that could play a big role in a Red Sox lineup as he looks to wrap balls around the Pesky Pole. But instead of this being an issue for the Red Sox and forcing them to figure out what to do with Contreras and Bauers, adding a player with this type of pop would never hurt. Even if the Red Sox want to ease Casas back into the lineup and he only plays about 100 games next season, if he can give the type of power production that we're used to seeing from him, and we all know that he has, the 26-year-old has a big future in Boston. That flexibility also helps Boston with injuries. Casas has missed a ton of time, and the Red Sox can't put all their eggs in one basket. With Bauers and Contreras here, any injury to him wouldn't hurt as much as it would have a couple of years ago. nigeria.title: INEC, security agencies addressing security concerns ahead of 2027 polls – Amupitan
nigeria.description: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, says the commission, in collaboration with security agencies, is taking necessary steps to address all security concerns ahead of the 2027 general elections. Amupitan ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​⁠‌‌‍‍‌‌​stated this on Saturday in Jos while speaking with newsmen during the monitoring of the ongoing mock accreditation. Addressing a question on the security challenge and the likely implications on voter participation, Amupitan said the safety of ad hoc staff and all Nigerians remained a priority to the commission. “As the chairman of INEC, I’m also worried about the state of security in Nigeria, but you can see we are taking some good steps to ensure that we nip it in the bud. “Just two days ago, we had a national security conference where we brought together all the members of the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES), the police, the military, the Civil Defence, and other paramilitary agencies. “So, we had a one-day conference where we discussed all these issues,” he said. Amupitan said that INEC had conducted a risk assessment of every part of Nigeria, using Election Risk Management (ERM) tools. “We have identified all the polling units that are vulnerable, and we have shared this with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extraordinary preparation for those places. “Any polling unit 500 meters from those vulnerable areas has been identified, and we are going to deal with it,” he said. Amupitan said the commission was interested in the security of the voters and ad hoc staff, particularly corps members. “It’s not every security matter you can bring to the open, but we are doing everything, both intelligence and physical, to ensure that the security on election day is assured,” he said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the monitoring of the mock accreditation exercise was still ongoing in different parts of the state as of the time of filling this report. nigeria.title: Referee faces suspension after punching goalkeeper in post-match rawl
nigeria.description: A Bolivian referee, Jordy Aleman, might face be faced with strict suspension rules after punching Real Potosi goalkeeper Cristian Martinez during a post-match confrontation following the 2026 Copa Bolivia final. The incident occurred on Wednesday after Always Ready secured the trophy with a 3-1 aggregate victory over Real Potosi. The second leg ended in a goalless draw at the Victor Agustin Ugarte Stadium in Potosi. Tensions flared after the final whistle as Real Potosi players approached Aleman to protest decisions made during the match. Television footage showed the referee punching Martinez in the face, triggering further disorder before police intervened to protect the officials. Reports from Spanish-language media, including MARCA, said the confrontation followed an insult directed at Aleman by the goalkeeper. Martinez reportedly told the referee, “I hope your mother dies.” Martinez later said the punch left his mouth bleeding. However, in a defiant response reported by El Diario, he remarked: “He should hit harder.” The goalkeeper also questioned Aleman’s professionalism and called for an exemplary punishment. He subsequently announced that he would not pursue legal action or file a formal complaint over the incident. In a statement shared by Spanish publication 20 Minutos, Martinez said: “My intention is to consider this episode over and avoid allowing this situation to continue generating conflict.” Aleman could face disciplinary sanctions under the Bolivian Football Federation’s Disciplinary Code, which reportedly provides for fines of at least 20 national minimum monthly salaries and bans of between one and three years for physical assaults. The incident also led to four Real Potosi players and three members of the club’s coaching staff reportedly receiving red cards. According to Bolivian publication Vision 360, the federation’s refereeing authorities are expected to review the incident alongside the match reports. Aleman’s status as an international referee could also have further implications. The referee has yet to make a public statement on the incident. nigeria.title: Meet Nigerian’s Maria Wophill named World Athletics’ Woman of the Year
nigeria.description: Veteran Nigerian sports administrator Maria Wophill has been named the World Athletics (WA) 2026 Woman of the Year in recognition of her decades-long contribution to gender equality and the development of women and girls in athletics. World Athletics announced the honour as part of its 2026 awards, recognising Wophill’s efforts to create opportunities for women in track and field through leadership, advocacy and grassroots development. Wophill previously served as secretary-general of the Athletics Federation of Nigeria (AFN) between 2005 and 2013. She has also held senior positions in the Federal Ministry of Youth and Sports Development and served on the World Athletics Women’s Committee from 2010 to 2018. Her contributions to Nigerian sports administration include advocacy for increased female representation on the boards of national sports federations, which helped secure additional positions for women. At the continental level, she championed the establishment of the Confederation of African Athletics (CAA) Gender Leadership Task Force in 2024. She has also mentored female coaches and sports administrators through the Women’s Sport Leadership Academy (WISH), while supporting grassroots participation through the Abuja FCT Girls Sprints and Relays, an initiative aimed at encouraging secondary school girls to take part in athletics. Reacting to the recognition, Wophill expressed gratitude to World Athletics and Nigerian sports organisations, describing the award as a motivation to continue contributing to the sport. “This has been a truly humbling year and I am very proud to be acknowledged for the work I have done,” she said. She added that the recognition had strengthened her commitment to promoting gender leadership, safeguarding young athletes and mentoring people within athletics. “This award has energised me to keep giving my best in all positions in athletics, with particular focus on gender leadership, safeguarding young athletes and mentoring within the sport,” she said. World Athletics President Sebastian Coe described Wophill as a deserving recipient, praising her efforts to improve female representation and mentor others in the sport. Her recognition is part of the 2026 World Athletics Awards, with the World Athletes of the Year, Rising Stars and Moment of the Year scheduled to be announced on Sunday. nigeria.title: Why Tinubu should stay in office for 10 years – Akande
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Former Osun State Governor, Bisi Akande, has called for President Bola Tinubu to remain in office for 10 years, saying the period would allow him to complete ongoing projects and deliver lasting reforms. Akande made the call during an interview on the Frankly Speaking with Icon podcast, published on Friday. “He should remain in office, if possible, for another 10 years; otherwise, we go back to the situation of ‘Ebinpawa’ because there has been a foundation for hunger,” Akande said. He cited the Olubadan’s comments on road projects across the South-West, including routes linking Ijebu-Ode, Abeokuta, Oyo and Ikire, as evidence of the administration’s ongoing work. Quoting the traditional ruler, Akande said: “If you are working like this, and this had not been done 50 years before you, what again do we still say you should do, and you have not done? “But so that you will be able to complete this good job that you started, Ibadan people and Oyo State people are supporting you to do another four years.” Akande also blamed successive military administrations for what he described as decades of neglect of agriculture, education and economic development, saying their policies contributed to the country’s present difficulties. “Forty years before he came, since 1966, when the military started ruling you, you have been laying the foundation for hunger. You have abandoned your farms. You have abandoned the job. You have refused to be educated. You have refused to be modernised,” he said. He expressed optimism that Tinubu’s policies would produce significant improvements in the coming years, particularly in electricity supply and modernisation. “So in another 10 years there will be electricity everywhere. There will be modernisation,” he said. “They liberalised electricity. If you have money today, you can create electricity in your home. You can create it in your city. You can create it around you,” he said. nigeria.description: Northwest University, Kano, has prohibited students and lecturers from giving or receiving gifts in connection with university services, warning that anyone who violates the directive will face disciplinary action. He also called on staff and students to take the directive seriously, adding, “A stitch in time saves nine!” Northwest University, Kano, is a state-owned institution established by the Kano State Government in 2012. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. “Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: NC State takes down Kansas State, 85-70
sports.description: RALEIGH, NC - NOVEMBER 19: Qadence Samuels #2 of the NC State Wolfpack shoots over Johnea Donahue #3 of the Georgetown Hoyas during the college basketball game between the Georgetown Hoyas and the NC State Wolfpack on November 19, 2026 at Reynolds Coliseum in Raleigh, NC. (Photo by Nicholas Faulkner/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The shots were falling for both teams on Friday night, which made for an entertaining back and forth that lasted about three quarters—before NC State finally seized control for good. It wasn’t exactly a defensive clinic for either team, not surprisingly, as both hit the 40-point mark in the first half. Wes Moore wasn’t super thrilled about the effort by his team on defense, but it did make for a fun half to watch. The Pack did get a bit better there in the second half, while Kansas State did not. The Wildcats played zone for the entire evening, mixing up some looks here and there, but mostly sticking with a 2-3 that left such spacious gaps that I’m sure Jim Boeheim was turning over in his grave. Qadence Samuels took advantage by doing her best Paul McNeil impression—she was 6-8 from three, and the team finished 10-15 from outside. As you can tell from that attempt total, NC State did not force the issue from the perimeter against K-State’s zone, mostly because that wasn’t necessary, as getting paint touches was still pretty easy. Zoe Brooks was back on the court for the first time in nearly three weeks and was back to her usual playmaking self, if maybe still a step slow. She had a beautiful dish to Khamil Pierre for a bucket to beat the third quarter horn that was part of an 11-0 run that put Kansas State in the rearview for good. That included the first seven points of the fourth quarter, five of which belonged to Brooks. The Pack ended up leading by double figures for the final nine minutes. Desiree Wooten put together another outstanding performance, scoring 21 points on 8-9 shooting; Khamil Pierre led all scorers with 23 points on 9-15 shooting. Samuels finished with 20. A good result for the Pack against a potential NCAA tournament team (K-State is No. 56 in Torvik), but the big test comes Saturday afternoon against LSU and the evil Mrs. SparkleFeathers.

sports.title: Luka Dončić gets in physical confrontation with fan
sports.description: Credit: Amazon Prime Video It was a bizarre scene in San Antonio as Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić got into a physical confrontation with a fan seated on the baseline. The Lakers held a 16-point halftime lead against the Spurs in their NBA Cup matchup on Friday night, but San Antonio rallied in the second half for a 99-96 victory. Dončić was visibly frustrated as he shot just 1-13 from downtown. He’s been scoring at such a historic rate this season that his 31 points were five off his season average. After the game was over and Luka was walking to the locker room, he took off his elbow band and threw it at a woman seated on the baseline who appeared to be yelling at him. Dončić then went back for the elbow band and the man seated next to her (presumably her husband or a significant other) then shoved Luka before a horde of people intervened to prevent the situation from escalating further. The camera above the backboard captured it all on the Amazon Prime Video telecast. A fan shoved Luka after he threw his band toward them https://t.co/AKh93Z9QUK — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) November 28, 2026 Luka Dončić is prone to the occasional outburst and his behavior has drawn criticism over the years at various points throughout his career . But this was a regrettable and bizarre incident that was easily preventable. The first fan was clearly letting Luka have it while walking to the locker room, but Dončić should know better and not engage by throwing anything at her. If he just ignored it, then none of what followed would have happened. Going back for the elbow band he threw was another strange decision. As for the male fan, you can appreciate him standing up for the lady, but there’s no excuse for ever putting your hands on a player. Thankfully it didn’t rise to Malice in the Palace levels or anything, but everyone was in the wrong here. sports.title: Red Sox's Triston Casas Could Force Interesting Lineup Decision Amid Return
sports.description: Red Sox's Triston Casas Could Force Interesting Lineup Decision Amid Return originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Red Sox have spent years trying to sort out their first base and designated hitter situation, hoping Triston Casas would eventually be the answer. Unfortunately for the Red Sox and Casas, injuries have derailed that a bit. As a result, the Red Sox have had to make moves, landing William Contreras last offseason and signing Jake Bauers this winter. A healthy Casas changes the lineup, especially if he can return to the player that we saw back in 2023. While the injuries certainly haven't helped Casas over the past couple of seasons now, there's no debating how good he was in 2023, hitting 24 home runs, 21 doubles, and driving in 65 runs. He returned to action in a winter ball game in the DR, playing Friday and hitting a grand slam. Casas also has a ton of upside. He has legitimate power in his left-handed bat that could play a big role in a Red Sox lineup as he looks to wrap balls around the Pesky Pole. But instead of this being an issue for the Red Sox and forcing them to figure out what to do with Contreras and Bauers, adding a player with this type of pop would never hurt. Even if the Red Sox want to ease Casas back into the lineup and he only plays about 100 games next season, if he can give the type of power production that we're used to seeing from him, and we all know that he has, the 26-year-old has a big future in Boston. That flexibility also helps Boston with injuries. Casas has missed a ton of time, and the Red Sox can't put all their eggs in one basket. With Bauers and Contreras here, any injury to him wouldn't hurt as much as it would have a couple of years ago. Henry Davis, a former first overall pick as a catcher, was traded on Friday in exchange for utility-man Tim Tawa . sports.title: “Not concerned” Arteta not paying attention to critics of Arsenal’s goals
sports.description: “Not concerned” Arteta not paying attention to critics of Arsenal’s goals Arsenal’s critics often question their attacking output, arguing that the Gunners do not score enough goals despite their consistent efforts to win matches. However, Mikel Arteta’s side have built their success on defensive organisation, meaning they do not always need to score several goals to secure victories. Their approach has attracted criticism from rival supporters and neutrals who prefer more expansive attacking football. Nevertheless, Arsenal have continued to deliver results, while some teams that adopt a more attacking approach struggle to achieve the same consistency. The Gunners have established themselves as one of the most consistent Premier League sides in recent seasons and are determined to challenge for the title again this campaign. Their priority remains finding ways to win, regardless of whether their performances satisfy every critic. Arteta responds to Arsenal’s goal scoring critics Arsenal are approaching an impressive milestone under Arteta, with the club set to reach 700 goals scored during his time in charge. That achievement challenges suggestions that his team consistently struggle to find the net. The Spaniard, however, is not interested in getting involved in arguments about statistics or outside opinions. His attention is firmly on preparing his players for their upcoming match against Manchester City . Asked about the criticism, according to Arsenal Media , Arteta said: “This is data and people have opinions or there will be moments about that, but I’m not concerned. I’m concerned about preparing the team to have the best possible mindset, energy, physical condition and clarity to beat City. That’s it.” (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Arsenal remain focused on winning Arteta’s response makes it clear that he has little interest in allowing criticism to distract his team. The winger left Sporting CP to join the City Football Academy in 2015 and spent eight years in east Manchester, despite not making his senior debut under Pep Guardiola. Forbs was primarily utilised in Manchester City ’s U21 side, for whom he made 38 appearances, scored 26 goals and provided 13 assists in a largely impressive spell a step down from the first-team. Additionally, Forbs managed to contribute to 47 goals in 34 appearances in the U18 group, while scoring five and assisting six in seven UEFA Youth League games for the Blues. (Photo by Marc Atkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund is preparing to dilute its Newcastle United shares by selling up to 25 percent of the club. The Guardian’s Matt Hughes reported that JP Morgan has been appointed to handle the process. That said, don’t panic. Everything points to PIF seeking outside investors only to help finance major infrastructure projects, including the building of a new stadium, instead of simply plotting a slow-cooked exit from Tyniside. PIF currently owns 84 percent of Newcastle, with the Reuben brothers holding the remaining 16 percent. A full 25 percent share issue would therefore significantly dilute PIF’s holding while leaving the Saudi fund as majority owner. PIF would retain 63 percent of NUFC after the sale, with the Reubens keeping their 16 percent and the newcomers owning 21 percent of the club and overtaking the latter in the Magpies power ladder. The development arrives amid ever-growing questions about PIF’s sporting portfolio. The fund already withdrew its support from LIV Golf, sold a stake in Al-Hilal and has reportedly shown willingness to dispose of other sporting assets, namely Newcastle—at least in the mind of some fans and outsiders. Those moves have fueled speculation that Newcastle could eventually be sold outright, but Hughes reported that PIF sources insist the fund “retain[s] a long-term commitment to Newcastle.” Newcastle declined to comment on the report. For now, therefore, the confirmed direction is a potential minority dilution rather than a complete PIF departure, even if the fund’s wider pullback from some sporting investments ensures scrutiny will continue. technology.title: Quantum: 'Five years, that's all we got…'
technology.description: SC26 in Chicago had the usual quantum booths, discussions, and hallway optimism. A lot of people were talking about integration with classical HPC and Slurm scheduling for quantum processors, co-design platforms, and GPU-accelerated error correction tools. That part is real and useful. What was harder to find was any result that changed the basic math on when quantum systems will actually do something a supercomputer can't already handle better. I had a long conversation in St. Louis (SC25) with a contact who works deep in quantum and has spent decades in HPC. He's not a skeptic for sport, although that can be fun, sure. Over a grifted free dinner in Chicago (the best kind), his take this year remains the same: the hype keeps outrunning the error rates. Quantum computers generate too many errors to give usable answers on anything interesting. Fixing that is the whole game. And that's a five-year game, minimum. Much like the Bowie anthem in the title. Qubits by the numbers There are two kinds of qubits. Physical qubits are the actual hardware: ions, superconducting circuits, and atoms in a trap. Logical qubits are the ones that do the computation. Each logical qubit is built out of many physical ones so the system can detect and correct errors while it runs. With the traditional surface-code approach, one logical qubit often needs somewhere between 500 and 2,000 physical qubits backing it up, depending on the hardware and the code. One logical qubit by itself is useless. Estimates for basic scientific modeling and small-scale simulation sit in the 100-to-500 logical-qubit range. Take the midpoint of 300. At the low end of the overhead that is 150,000 physical qubits. At the high end it is several million. That is only for early science. Commercial work like molecular mapping for pharma, large optimization problems, complex financial models, pushes into the thousands of logical qubits. National-security and encryption-related work sits even higher. Those numbers have not magically shrunk. A system that can map a modestly sized drug molecule, or run a materials simulation that is still too slow on classical machines, is the kind of workload people actually mean when they talk about useful quantum advantage. Until the logical-qubit counts get there with error rates low enough to finish the job, those problems stay on the machines we already know how to build. Ok, so let's just scale it up This is the world of HPC, we know how to scale stuff, right? Yes, but this isn't a matter of adding a few more racks. Scaling to an additional few hundred thousand physical qubits is not a rack or two or ten. It's probably a dedicated building with its own cryogenics, control electronics, and power draw that is still measured in megawatts even before you get useful logical capacity. technology.title: Unkernel and Trynix just transported computing to 2035
technology.description: What's the difference between just-for-fun demo hacks, and serious carefully designed large-scale software architecture? It's the quick-and-dirty jobs that end up transforming computing. A blog post earlier this week called 2035 came early led the Reg FOSS desk down what we thought was a fascinating, and possibly quite scary, rabbit-hole… but it turned out to be an entire warren. We thought we were still in 2026, but in turns out that in some ways, tech just leaped forward a decade. To try to convey the point of this blog post – why what had been just a fun clever little hack has the potential to take half a century of OS and hypervisor design and throw it out of the nearest window – will take quite a lot of unpacking. If you bear with us, we will try to walk you through it. To get started, we need to go back a decade or more. Stick with this: there are laughs, as well as hammers taken to beloved ideas. The year of 2035 and the ideas around that come from a remarkable talk by Gary Bernhardt of Destroy All Software, which is both funny and highly educational. It will really massively assist understanding what this article and the technology is all about if you have the time to watch the talks. The Reg FOSS desk is not at all fond of spoken-word video as a medium – we much prefer to read than listen – but the three talks we're going to mention are golden, among the very best presentations this century in all of computing and IT. Seriously, they are worth your time. As a preface, before we go into Bernhardt's half-hour information-dense talk, let's warm up with a four-minute funny one. But first, let's look at the context for that. Step 0: JavaScript is the language of web programming In 2009, Jeff Atwood laid this out in an article called All Programming is Web Programming . It's still coming true today. Software is getting very blurred around the edges. The entire SaaS industry means that massive organizations run on web apps. Tech like Electron embeds a web browser inside JavaScript apps built in Node.js, while Progressive Web Apps make websites look like local program windows. The most popular desktop Linux in the world is ChromeOS Flex, which doesn't support local native applications at all. Everything is browser windows, even the desktop. It's all built in JavaScript. And yet… Step 1: JavaScript is kind of weird and kind of bad. Bernhardt made this case in 2012, with a celebrated lightning talk called Wat , from the CodeMash conference in 2012. Wat walks through a whole list of examples of how JavaScript is a very strange programming language and does very strange things that are not at all what you might expect. Some of the jokes will make more sense to programmers, but we reckon anyone who has ever fought with a recalcitrant bit of software will get some laughs from it – and that probably applies to all readers of The Register. Step 2: JavaScript is in the process of conquering the world. Bernhardt moved on to much bigger ideas at PyCon 2014

science.title: Space in Macy’s 100 Thanksgiving Day parades
science.description: null The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is sure to be a blast, but it is a bit light on "space." According to previews provided by the department store chain, the founder of the New York City holiday celebration, space fans turning up or tuning in to catch sight of an astronaut or other nod to NASA will have only a returning rocket to look forward to on Saturday (Nov. 28). (The parade has been postponed two days from Thursday, Nov. 26, due to bad weather.) Not that Macy's (or the space agency) has hinted about anything cosmic planned for the 100th parade; it's only that the event has had a long history of celebrating space exploration with its floats and balloons. "For our 100th parade, we're creating a celebration of unprecedented scale and will deliver an unforgettable Thanksgiving for millions across the country," said Sharon Otterman, Macy's chief marketing officer, in a statement . First held in 1924 for Macy's colleagues, their friends and families, the Thanksgiving Day Parade has been held every year with the exception of a three-year break during World War II. Spanning longer than the dawn of the Space Age, the space race and NASA's entire 68-year history, the celebration has integrated space themes into its displays, even before the first rocket flew beyond Earth's atmosphere . Weighty weightless man The earliest space-themed feature of the parade may have been the "Space Ship," a float that made its first appearance in the 19th procession in 1945 and in various configurations — with and without astronauts and planets — appeared on and off through 1962. Perhaps more memorable, though, and certainly much larger, was the "Spaceman" (or, more appropriately, "The Giant Spaceman"). The 70-foot-long (21-meter) helium balloon made its debut in 1952, nine years before the Soviet Union's Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space. Described by Macy's as an "artist's conception of a visitor from another planet," the humanoid figure had a black spacesuit , a silver helmet and boots, a jet propulsion backpack and a black rocket gun. Once the heaviest balloon in the parade, the "Spaceman" was created by the Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company years before anyone had entered space. (Image credit: Macy's) Ironically, for a figure garbed for the weightless environment of space, the Spaceman was for a long time the parade's heaviest giant balloon. At 600 pounds (272 kilograms), it was only tied by the Pink Panther in 1988 and then exceeded two years later by Bart Simpson. The rubber Spaceman was created by Goodyear Tire, the same company that contributed hardware to NASA's Apollo program , including the wire mesh non-pneumatic tires for the lunar roving vehicle. The Spaceman survived being torn when it was caught with a lamppost in 1955, and a helium shortage resulting in it and other balloons being filled with air and held up by cranes in 1958. science.title: 12 grains of dust found high in Earth's atmosphere reveal secrets of water at the edge of the solar system
science.description: A dozen grains of dust that have wandered in from the distant Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune were found floating in Earth's stratosphere. And it turns out they hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be surprisingly abundant in the outer solar system. When analyzed by a team of scientists the 12 dust grains, which were captured by NASA's stratospheric ER-2 research aircraft, show signs of having interacted with a form of water that contains heavy oxygen isotopes. This is important because to better understand how the planets formed, scientists are seeking to understand how various materials were distributed around the early solar system 4.5 billion years ago. If there is a reservoir of heavy water out in the solar system's hinterlands, understanding how that water got out there and stayed out there will inform models that describe the growth of the planets. Water consists of two hydrogen atoms and an oxygen atom. What we usually refer to as heavy water is water that contains a heavy isotope of hydrogen. An isotope is an atom that contains the usual number of protons for that element, but a different number of neutrons . Elements are determined by the number of protons they contain. For example, hydrogen always has just one proton. Ordinary 'light' hydrogen has 1 proton and no neutrons, but its heavy isotopes – deuterium and tritium – contain 1 and 2 neutrons, respectively, in addition to the proton. However, there's another kind of water that features heavy isotopes of oxygen instead. Ordinary 'light' oxygen is made from 8 protons and 8 neutrons and is hence known as oxygen-16 but some oxygen isotopes can have 9 or 10 neutrons, and we call these isotopes oxygen-17 or -18. There have been a few clues that such a reservoir exists. Mineralogical evidence from a single carbonaceous chondritic meteorite and measurements from comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko indicated the presence of minerals that had formed from interactions between silicate rock and abundant oxygen-heavy variety of water, but it was not clear whether these were isolated instances or a clue to something more widespread. An illustration comparing the locations of the solar system planets to the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud, a theorized shell of icy objects at the farthest reaches of our solar system. (Image credit: ESA) Another data point comes from NASA's Genesis mission, which launched in 2001 and collected particles from the solar wind that were subsequently returned to Earth for study. The analysis of these particles indicated that the sun contains proportionally more ordinary 'light' oxygen than Earth and most meteorites. This suggests that there could be an outwards gradient of increasing abundance of heavy oxygen. Yet the Kuiper Belt is so far away that it makes finding more evidence for this difficult. science.title: Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still
science.description: null Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone. The five stars are still there, but the shape you may have memorized looks like it's been picked up and turned over. It looks more like an E or an M, depending on when you look. Now try and look for the Big Dipper /the Plough. It's gone. Nothing mysterious has happened, of course. Cassiopeia is doing exactly what it always does, but it's a reminder that the northern sky is where you can easily watch the stars move — and the seasons turn. What's happening and when to look Stars move anti-clockwise around the north celestial pole, so Cassiopeia changes orientation. (Image credit: Alan Dyer/Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) Late November is an excellent time to reacquaint yourself with Cassiopeia from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. Look high in the northern sky during the evening for its five prominent stars — Caph, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah and Segin. Depending on exactly when you look, it can look like a W, E, M or a 3. This is because Cassiopeia is circumpolar. Rather than rising in the east and eventually setting in the west like many familiar constellations , it circles the north celestial pole — a position currently held by Polaris , the North Star. From sufficiently northerly latitudes, its main stars never disappear below the horizon. This gives us a simple observing experiment. Find Cassiopeia in the early evening and remember its orientation relative to the horizon. Go back several hours later and look again. The constellation has moved around Polaris, and its shape has changed. The stars haven't changed their arrangement — Earth has simply rotated from west to east. We all know this logically, but watching the familiar pattern of Cassiopeia's stars apparently tip over during a single night makes Earth's rotation a lot less abstract. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 27, 1885: Astronomer captures 1st known photo of a meteor during an Andromedid meteor storm
science.description: null On Nov. 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor. The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek. He captured the trail of the meteor on a photographic plate in the Czech Republic. The meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower . The Andromedids were associated with Biela's Comet , which broke apart in the 1850s. When Weinek observed the meteor shower in 1885, it was in the middle of a meteor storm . This means that there were way more meteors than usual. Skywatchers could see thousands of meteors per hour. The November 1872 incidence of the Andromedid meteor shower, as seen over France, in a painting. (Image credit: Alto Vintage Images/Alamy) Why it mattered Not many stargazers may be be acquainted with the Andromedid meteor shower. What used to be a spectacular annual meteor shower is now hardly even visible. But in 1885, the Andromedids were an annual treat for skywatchers hoping for a chance to see the remains of Biela's comet (a comet first spotted in 1772 and then found - for the third time - in 1826 by the German astronomer Wilhelm von Biela, from whom it gets its name). Meteor Shower Quiz: How Well Do You Know 'Shooting Stars'? This modern photo of the Geminid meteor shower shows dozens of meteors captured in a long exposure by Josh Drury. Ladislaus Weinek, who captured the first photo of a meteor, had to use a photographic plate in 1889. (Image credit: Josh Dury) Camera technology has come a long way since 1885, which is good since it is a bit harder to see the Andromedids these days. Instead of photographic plates or digital cameras, astronomers now have to use special tracking equipment to record images of Andromedid meteors. In 2011, astronomers announced that the meteor shower seemed to be undergoing a resurgence of activity, with 50 meteors per hour, and upticks were expected in 2018 and 2023. Want more space history? science.description: null Astronomers witnessed the spectacular cosmic indigestion that resulted from a red giant star that devoured a stellar Bao bun in the form of its smaller companion star. That isn't a random comparison. The cannibal star, which is 350 times bigger than the sun, is nicknamed "Big Bao," while its unfortunate companion had the nickname "Little Bao." The cute cosmic monikers come from the fact that this destructive merger event has been designated AT2025abao. A Bao bun might be a little snack for a human, but this red giant star made a real meal out of Little Bao. This cannibalistic event was tracked by a wide array of ground- and space-based telescopes, including NASA space missions NEOWISE, SPHEREx, and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), as well as the W. M. Keck Observatory in Hawaii. The conclusion of the event AT2025abao was marked by a massive eruption witnessed in Oct. 2025 by two instruments at Caltech's Palomar Observatory: the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) and the Wide-field INfrared Transient ExploreR (WINTER). "The excitement was real," team member Viraj Karambelkar of Columbia University said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. "We couldn't quite believe our luck. With detailed observations for several years before the merger, for the first time, we now have an unprecedented glimpse of the conditions that lead to such cosmic events." Reconstructing a violent cosmic collision The story of AT2025abao began when astronomers detected a bright flash in the nearby Andromeda galaxy , a region where scientists hadn't expected to see a cosmic explosion. Responding to this unexpected flash, Karambelkar and colleagues set about investigating its cause with a plethora of telescopes. This led to them seeing a slow and continuous brightening over the course of two years, They determined the cause of the flash was a rare stellar merger, the luminous red nova now designated AT2025abao. Thus, the team determined that at the heart of the event is a red giant, a star that puffs out to hundreds of times its original size after it runs out of hydrogen in its core. science.title: New Scientist Book Club: How urine changed the course of human history
science.description: A detail from Joseph Wright’s 1771 painting The Alchemist Discovering Phosphorus, showing Henning Brand in 1669 Science History Images/Alamy Imagine you could boil the development of science down to a single ingredient. A magical, mystical compound that transformed human history. Of course, science doesn’t work that way; even if breakthroughs shift the paradigm of our understanding, discovery doesn’t progress like a tech tree in a computer game, but as an interweaving tapestry of complementary and competing ideas and experimentation. Theories can bubble under the surface for centuries, overlooked because of politics or failure to realise their implications, while innovations can emerge from taking an idea in one industry and transplanting it to another. But, for a moment, try and picture what just one such ingredient could be. What would you pick? For centuries, in medieval Europe, alchemists quested for the “Philosopher’s Stone” that would finally help them achieve their dreams of transmutation. It was a search doomed to failure from the very beginning. And yet, a far better idea was under their noses – or, rather, their underpants – the entire time. My pick? Urine has a strong case for being the most transformative substance in human history. Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter The development of civilisation was built on chemistry. It required the first chemical reaction we mastered – fire – to keep us warm, cook our food and smelt ores. But leatherwork played an equally key role. Urine is a source of urea, which bacteria can break down into ammonia, granting early humans easy access to a base that could soften organic matter and tan hides. Across the world, leatherwork became the cornerstone of survival for every civilisation, from the Americas to Europe, Africa and Asia: even cultures that didn’t develop a bronze age, such as the Aztec, or skipped it entirely, as seen in Sub-Saharan Africa, relied on leatherwork for clothes, structures, industry and commerce. In ancient Rome, urine was so useful for laundries to keep togas whiter-than-white that Emperor Vespasian levied a tax on draining urinals. At first, the raider was frustrated; scavenging the tombs near Thebes, he had hoped to uncover a priceless heirloom, or a nugget of gold that would sparkle with lustre in the starlight. Instead, he had found only a clutch of rolled scrolls, made of papyrus and sealed against the elements. For a moment, he considered casting the documents aside and leaving them for the desert. Then greed got the better of him. Westerners loved all things Egyptian, he reasoned. Since the French had arrived with Napoleon, the new field of “Egyptology” had swept the continent, capturing the imagination of scholars and the wealthy. It was almost as popular as the new science of “chemistry”. Surely, if he took his find to the market, he’d find some gullible fool willing to buy it. The buyer’s name was Jean d’Anastasy, and he was anything but a fool. Born in Greece as the son of a Damascus merchant who had won and lost his fortune in the Napoleonic Wars, d’Anastasy had used his family’s connections to set himself up as a grain merchant in Alexandria, before scheming his way into being named the local Consul General for Sweden and Norway. When the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured this image on November 8, 2026, clouds encroached on the snowy mountain on Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula . But they hovered beneath the volcano’s 3,283-meter (10,771-foot) peak, leaving a clear opening over its caldera and northern upper slopes. The upper reaches of Shivelyuch feature a caldera 9 kilometers (5.6 miles) wide that is open to the south. A lava dome , formed by vents extruding viscous magma, appears as a dark area within it. Lava domes on Shivelyuch go through cycles of growth and collapse, with collapses sometimes setting off fast-moving avalanches of hot ash and rock called pyroclastic flows . In November 2026, effusive eruptions of lava and explosive activity at Shivelyuch had been ongoing for months , according to reports from the Kamchatka Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT). And despite frequent cloudiness, satellites regularly detect thermal anomalies from the volcano. On the day of this image, KVERT reported that a plume of resuspended ash drifted 120 kilometers (75 miles) to the east. That kind of activity is relatively tame for the mountain. Explosions from Shivelyuch periodically send ash several kilometers up into the atmosphere, where it can travel great distances and pose risks to aircraft . In July 2026, an ash plume rode the jet stream over the Bering Sea into Alaskan airspace, according to news reports , prompting the cancellation of multiple flights. science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales". After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp? Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters. They gave him freedom to tell the story he wanted to tell, and he landed on a not obviously box-office-friendly formula of "No dying, no fighting, no shooting, no photon torpedoes, no phaser blasts, no stereotypical bad guy". It was a massive shift away from Khan and Kruge, the grandstanding villains in movies II and III. Nimoy also wanted the film to have an environmental message and appeal beyond the franchise's traditional fanbase. The film would actually be promoted with minimal "Trek" branding in some territories. (Image credit: Paramount) "I wanted to make it accessible to people who don't go to 'Star Trek' movies," Nimoy said in "The Fifty-Year Mission" by Edward Gross and Mark A. Altman.
